Header: 2026-01-28 15:00 PST | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Tina Park (Redwood SE), Ravi Kapoor (Hypatia - Head ML), Elena Morales (Hypatia PM), Samir Patel (Hypatia Infra)

00:00 Alyssa Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off in a minute, looks like folks are rolling in
00:18 Elena Morales: hi hi, sorry running a bit behind on my side
00:25 Alyssa Chen: no worries, we'll give two minutes, want to make sure we cover success metrics and the open model shortlist today
00:40 Marco Ruiz: quick agenda: 1) current stack & constraints, 2) POC success criteria, 3) model shortlist + tradeoffs, 4) sizing/benchmarks and timeline
00:52 Ravi Kapoor: great thanks, quick context — Hypatia is building a legal research assistant, lots of domain docs (court rulings, contracts), multilingual support for EN/ES/FR, and PII redaction needs
01:08 Samir Patel: infra constraints: VPC-only for PII samples, we have GCP and on-prem colocation for heavier runs, but initially want Redwood hosted perf tests with redacted data
01:25 Tina Park: noted — VPC and private deployment conversation later in the POC if baseline looks good
01:33 Alyssa Chen: high-level success criteria from Redwood side — what are you measuring? Elena?
01:38 Elena Morales: primary is QA accuracy on our legal Q/A set — target is >= 85% exact-match or acceptable precision/recall across 500 evals; also p95 latency under 200ms for single-turn retrieval-augmented prompts; throughput target ~100 req/s peak, average 20-30 req/s; cost per 1k tokens under our budget TBD
02:05 Marco Ruiz: just to clarify — 200ms p95 is aggressive for larger models, we can try request routing and quantized variants, maybe aim first for 300ms then optimize
02:14 Ravi Kapoor: yeah we can be flexible, but user UX expects snappy responses for short queries; for longer multi-paragraph answers we can tolerate more latency
02:29 Alyssa Chen: on evaluation metric — do you have a scoring harness or labels?
02:33 Elena Morales: yes we have a labeled set of 500 Q/A pairs and a separate 200 for spot checks, we can share by next week
02:42 Marco Ruiz: perfect, that helps benchmarks. Now model shortlist we suggested: Llama2-13B-az (typo sometimes), Llama-3-13B (open variants), Falcon-40B-instruct, Mistral-Instruct-7B, and an OpenLLaMA 3x variant — we'll also try quantized 4-bit runs. Tradeoffs: smaller models easier latency/cost but risk domain hallucination
03:10 Ravi Kapoor: any Redwood-verified profiles for these? We've seen Redwood posts about "Redwood-verified" but curious about in-house numbers
03:17 Alyssa Chen: yes we have perf profiles and earlier test artifacts; Marco can run a baseline with our infra to produce p95 and throughput numbers for the shortlisted models — expect variance by prompt length and context window
03:30 Marco Ruiz: quick note — KV cache behavior matters for multi-turn legal QAs, we should set up a prefix caching test; also batching config will impact p95, so we'll benchmark steady-state and burst scenarios
03:46 Samir Patel: about data privacy — if we share unredacted samples for model quality we need to do it inside VPC or with redaction; we'll try redacted sample first and escalate to VPC connection if needed
03:59 Elena Morales: we also need multilingual QA — Spanish and French. How do these open models perform cross-lingually?
04:08 Marco Ruiz: smaller Llama variants degrade on non-English, Mistral tends to be weaker in FR/ES unless finetuned; Falcon-40B has decent multi-lingual, but costs and latency higher. We can include a small bilingual eval set in the 500 to measure drop-off.
04:28 Alyssa Chen: timeline proposal: Week 0 (this week) — kickoff + data handoff; Week 1 — baseline runs (latency/throughput/quality) on 3 models; Week 2 — targeted optimizations (quant, cache, batching) and rerun; Week 3 — customer evals and integration tests; Week 4 — final report and recommendation. Total ~4 weeks
04:50 Ravi Kapoor: fits our PM timeline if benchmarks look promising. What about dedicated vs hosted? If throughput grows we may need Dedicated with reserved pools
04:58 Marco Ruiz: yes early POC on hosted is fastest; if you need predictable SLOs and VPC routing we can propose Redwood Dedicated or Private. We'll capture cost delta in the POC pricing doc
05:12 Elena Morales: success criteria recap: 85% QA, p95 < 200-300ms (TBD), peak 100 req/s, multilingual parity within 10% of EN baseline, and integration with our document store for retrieval augmentation
05:30 Alyssa Chen: good. Benchmarks: Marco will run two types: 1) quality-only (single user sequential run, measure accuracy/LM scoring), 2) load test (concurrent users, throughput, p95/p99 latency). We'll also test retrieval-augmented prompts using a 1-3 doc context window to simulate real usage
05:52 Marco Ruiz: for the load test I propose a synthetic traffic generator to simulate 100 req/s with realistic token lengths (short queries ~50 tokens, long answers ~400 tokens)
06:08 Samir Patel: we can provide a staging vector db endpoint for retrieval tests, credentials via secure share
06:15 Alyssa Chen: noted — please add to the POC doc. any security/compliance asks?
06:21 Ravi Kapoor: SOC 2 and audit logs required; also SSO (SAML) for any dashboard access and role-based access for logs. Can you share Redwood's SOC doc?
06:31 Alyssa Chen: yes, we'll attach SOC2 report and our security whitepaper. Also we can enable audit logging and token-level traces for the POC if needed
06:43 Elena Morales: pricing — can you provide a rough run-rate estimate for the 4-week POC and an annual committed price if we go Dedicated?
06:50 Alyssa Chen: we'll include ballpark estimates in the POC plan; it's usage-based for hosted with Dedicated pricing as a commit overlay. Marco will add performance impact notes per model so you can weigh cost vs accuracy
07:05 Marco Ruiz: one more technical note — if you plan to use streaming for user UX we should test both streaming throughput and chunked responses; some quantized kernels affect streaming latency
07:18 Ravi Kapoor: good call. Also can we do a small finetune on top of an open model as part of the POC? say 1-2 epoch on domain doc samples?
07:26 Marco Ruiz: feasible but heavier; finetune/delta tuning on 13B can be done quickly with adapters, might add 1 week depending on compute. We can scope a short adapter experiment in Week 2 if you want
07:39 Elena Morales: let's prioritize baseline + optimizations first; if quality shortfalls remain we'll revisit adapter tuning
07:45 Alyssa Chen: OK so deliverables: POC plan + benchmark sheet (Alyssa), baseline runs (Marco), data share (Hypatia). We'll put dates in the doc.
07:58 Ravi Kapoor: anything else?
08:02 Tina Park: just a note that we'll capture models attempted incl quant/4-bit/8-bit and settings so it's reproducible
08:10 Elena Morales: perfect. Thanks everyone. we'll look for the POC plan and dataset link.
08:16 Alyssa Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invite for 2026-02-10 benchmark review
08:23 (call ends)
